_meta.scope: Public US grocery peers of Sprouts Farmers Market (SFM). SEC filings only, except SKU counts where noted. Whole Foods is excluded (another agent covers it).
_meta.units: net_sales in USD millions. Percentages are plain numbers (7.3 = 7.3%). Store counts are at fiscal year end.

conventions.derived: Listed in each year's 'derived' array: computed by us from reported figures (ratios, store growth, net new stores, average square feet). It was not stated by the company in that form.
conventions.null: Not disclosed in the sources we checked. Nothing was estimated or interpolated.
conventions.gross_margin_pct / operating_margin_pct: When the company reports a rate we give that rate. Otherwise we compute it from the income statement and list it in 'derived'. 'gm_basis' and 'om_basis' state the scope (company or segment) and the denominator.
conventions.fiscal_year labels: Each company's own label. FY ends differ (see fiscal_year_end). WMT labels its year by the January it ends (FY2026 = Feb 2025-Jan 2026). KR, ACI and TGT label it by the calendar year it starts in (KR FY2025 = Feb 2025-Jan 2026).

SFM.fiscal_year_end: 52/53 weeks ending the Sunday closest to Dec 31 (FY2025 ended Dec 28, 2025). FY2026 is a 53-week year.
SFM.product_focus: Specialty natural/organic grocer in a 'flipped' farmers-market layout: produce at the center (~20% of selling space), curated better-for-you assortment, vitamins, bulk, no fuel or pharmacy.
SFM.comp_definition: Comparable store sales: a store's sales are included from the first day of its 61st week after opening or acquisition. Closed stores are excluded from the day of closure. Total sales; e-commerce is not carved out and fuel does not apply.

skus_per_store.note: Not disclosed in the 10-K. The 10-K says it 'launched more than 7,000 new products' in 2025. Trade press cites ~18,000-20,000 SKUs per store, but we could not verify that against a primary or dated reputable source, so it is left null.

fiscal_years.gm_basis: company, GP/net sales (cost of sales includes DC and supply-chain costs and their D&A)

fiscal_years.private_label_note: 'just over 23% of our revenue'. Two relocations are excluded from openings.

latest_quarter.guidance: FY2026 (52-week basis): net sales growth ~4.3%, comps ~(1.7)%, EBIT ~$605M, 42 net new stores. Q4 comps (2.0)% to (4.0)%. The 53rd week adds ~$190M of sales.

NGVC.company: Natural Grocers by Vitamin Cottage, Inc.
NGVC.fiscal_year_end: September 30. FY2026 ended 2026-09-30. Its 10-K was not yet filed on 2026-11-23, so FY2026 comes from the 8-K earnings release of 2026-11-19.
NGVC.product_focus: Small-box (~11,000 selling sq ft) natural and organic grocer with strict product standards (100% organic produce) and a large dietary-supplement department (~6,500 supplement SKUs). No fuel or pharmacy.
NGVC.comp_definition: DAILY AVERAGE comparable store sales: comparable store sales divided by the number of days in the period. A store enters the comp base on the first day of its 13th full month after opening. Remodeled or relocated stores stay in the base. The same stores are compared for the same number of operating months.

skus_per_store.note: 'an average of approximately 20,000 SKUs ... per comparable store', including ~6,500 dietary-supplement SKUs (FY2025 10-K)

fiscal_years.gm_basis: company, GP after product AND store occupancy costs / net sales
fiscal_years.note: The release states 7 openings and 175 stores at year end, which implies 1 closure. Square footage is not in the release.

fiscal_years.avg_store_sqft_note: SELLING sq ft average as disclosed ('approximately 11,000'). Gross sq ft average is 16,188 (2,735,774/169), derived.
GROSS sq ft / stores (2,728,203/169), derived. Not comparable with the FY2025 selling-sq-ft figure.

latest_quarter.guidance: FY2027 outlook: 7 to 9 new stores, 2 to 4 relocations/remodels, daily average comps +2.0% to +3.0%, diluted EPS $2.03-$2.10, capex $55-60M. Long-term target 4-5% annual unit growth.

KR.fiscal_year_end: Saturday nearest Jan 31. FY2025 = 52 weeks ended 2026-01-31. FY2023 = 53 weeks ended 2024-02-03.
KR.scope: Total company. Sales include supermarket fuel, pharmacy, eCommerce and (in FY2024 and earlier) Kroger Specialty Pharmacy.
KR.product_focus: Conventional supermarkets under many local banners: full assortment, most with pharmacy (2,250 of 2,697) and many with fuel centers (1,731), plus food production plants and a large private-label program.
KR.comp_definition: IDENTICAL sales EXCLUDING FUEL: sales to retail customers from all departments at identical supermarkets, plus Delivery. A supermarket is identical once it has operated without expansion or relocation for five full quarters. Kroger Delivery sales from fulfillment centers count if the delivery is in an existing Kroger supermarket geography. FY2025 and FY2024 are shown 'excluding Adjusted Items' (Colorado labor-dispute stores removed for 4 weeks of Q1). FY2024 is on a 52-week basis.

skus_per_store.note: Total SKUs per store are not disclosed. The 10-K says supermarkets 'on average, stock over 13,000 private label items' (FY2025). Prior years: over 12,000 (FY2024), 12,600 (FY2023).

fiscal_years.gm_basis: company. Kroger gross margin = sales minus merchandise costs incl. advertising, warehousing and transportation. EXCLUDES rent and D&A. Includes fuel.
fiscal_years.om_basis: company GAAP operating profit / sales. Includes $2.5B of fulfillment-network impairment and related charges. Adjusted FIFO operating profit was $4.9B.
fiscal_years.avg_store_sqft_note: Total supermarket sq ft of 180M (rounded) / 2,697, derived
fiscal_years.private_label_note: DERIVED: 'Our Brands' 'over $39 billion' / total sales (incl. fuel). The $39B definition includes fresh and service-case products not carrying a Kroger brand, which explains much of the jump from $32B. Treat as approximate and not comparable year over year.
DERIVED: Our Brands 'over $32 billion' / total sales
fiscal_years.src: KR_10K_FY2025 (stores, comps); KR_10K_FY2024 (GM rate, Our Brands)

fiscal_years.gm_basis: company, as presented in the FY2024 10-K. The FY2023 10-K originally showed 22.24%; we use the later presentation.
fiscal_years.om_basis: company GAAP. Includes $1.5B of opioid settlement charges.

latest_quarter.comp_note: Identical sales without fuel. Includes a ~138 bp headwind from the Inflation Reduction Act drug-price provisions.
latest_quarter.stores_note: Not disclosed in the Q2 10-Q or the release. Rolling 4 quarters: 35 supermarkets opened, expanded, relocated or acquired.
latest_quarter.guidance: FY2026 identical sales without fuel lowered to 0.2%-0.8% (from 1.0%-2.0%) on 2026-09-11. Adjusted EPS and FIFO operating profit guidance reaffirmed. No store-opening guidance in filings. Pending acquisition of Giant Eagle announced 2026-07-01.

ACI.fiscal_year_end: Last Saturday in February. FY2025 = 53 weeks ended 2026-02-28. FY2024 = 52 weeks ended 2025-02-22. FY2023 = 52 weeks ended 2024-02-24. Q1 is 16 weeks; Q2-Q4 are 12 weeks.
ACI.scope: Total company. 'Net sales and other revenue' includes fuel and pharmacy.
ACI.product_focus: Conventional food and drug supermarkets (Safeway, Albertsons, Vons, Jewel-Osco and others; 22 banners): full assortment, ~1,700 in-store pharmacies, ~400 fuel centers.
ACI.comp_definition: IDENTICAL sales EXCLUDING FUEL: stores operating during the same period in both years, compared on a DAILY basis. Direct-to-consumer digital sales are INCLUDED. Acquired stores become identical one year after acquisition.

skus_per_store.note: Not disclosed per store. The Own Brands portfolio offers 'more than 14,000 unique items' company-wide (FY2025 10-K).

fiscal_years.gm_basis: company. Cost of sales includes purchasing, inbound freight, warehousing and distribution, and digital delivery and handling. Includes fuel and LIFO.
fiscal_years.om_basis: company GAAP operating income / net sales and other revenue
fiscal_years.avg_store_sqft_note: Total retail sq ft of 112.0M / 2,244, derived
fiscal_years.private_label_note: DERIVED: 'Own Brands retail sales of $16.9 billion' / net sales and other revenue

latest_quarter.guidance: WITHDRAWN. On 2026-10-13 the company said it is 'no longer providing a fiscal 2026 outlook' pending a comprehensive business review in Q4. Seven new stores opened in the first 28 weeks of FY2026.

PUBLIX.company: Publix Super Markets, Inc. (employee-owned. Stock is not exchange-traded, but the company is an SEC filer.)
PUBLIX.fiscal_year_end: Last Saturday in December. FY2025 = 52 weeks ended 2025-12-27. FY2024 = 2024-12-28. FY2023 = 2023-12-30 (52 weeks). FY2022 was 53 weeks.
PUBLIX.scope: Total company, single segment (Southeast US). net_sales = 'Sales', which excludes other operating income. XBRL 'Revenues' (e.g. $63,209M in FY2025) includes it.
PUBLIX.product_focus: Conventional full-service supermarkets in 8 Southeast states: full perishables (~47% of sales) and grocery, with in-store pharmacy. Prototypes are 32,000-62,000 sq ft.
PUBLIX.comp_definition: Comparable store sales = supermarkets open for the same weeks in both periods, INCLUDING replacement supermarkets. Sales of supermarkets replaced on site are classified as new-store sales. Total sales; fuel is not material.

skus_per_store.note: Not disclosed in filings. No dated reputable figure found.

fiscal_years.gm_basis: company, sales less cost of merchandise sold / sales (LIFO). Ex-LIFO 25.5%.
fiscal_years.om_basis: company operating profit / sales. Operating profit includes other operating income.
fiscal_years.avg_store_sqft_note: 67.8M sq ft of supermarket space / 1,432, derived

latest_quarter.comp_note: 9 months: -0.4%. Hit by the Medicare maximum fair price drug-price change effective 2026-01-01.
latest_quarter.guidance: Publix gives no comp or earnings guidance. FY2026 capex expected ~$2.4B (10-K FY2025). 9M 2026: 23 opened (7 replacements), 12 closed.

COST.fiscal_year_end: Sunday nearest Aug 31. FY2026 = 52 weeks ended 2026-08-30. FY2025 = 52 weeks ended 2025-08-31. FY2024 = 52 weeks ended 2024-09-01. FY2023 = 53 weeks. Q4 is 16 weeks. FY2026 is the latest completed year, so the three years are FY2026, FY2025 and FY2024.
COST.scope: Mixed. net_sales and gross margin are TOTAL COMPANY. The US segment ('United States' incl. Puerto Rico) is given separately as total revenue (incl. membership fees) and operating income. Warehouse counts are given for both US and total.
COST.product_focus: Membership warehouse club: limited assortment (<4,000 active SKUs) in bulk sizes across food and sundries, fresh, and non-foods, plus gas, pharmacy, optical and food court. Food (Foods and Sundries + Fresh Foods) is ~53% of net sales.
COST.comp_definition: Comparable sales = net sales from warehouses open more than one year, including remodels, relocations and expansions, plus e-commerce sites operating more than one year. Reported WITH gasoline and FX. The 'adjusted' figure excludes changes in gasoline prices and FX. The 10-K rounds to whole percent; the precise figures below come from the Q4 8-Ks.

skus_per_store.note: 'We carry less than 4,000 active stock keeping units (SKUs) per warehouse in our core warehouse business'. Also 9,000-11,000 SKUs online.

fiscal_years.net_sales_note: Total company net sales, excluding $5,907M of membership fees. US segment total revenue was $219,823M.
fiscal_years.gm_basis: TOTAL COMPANY, (net sales - merchandise costs) / net sales. Excludes membership fees. Merchandise costs include fresh-food department labor.
fiscal_years.om_basis: US SEGMENT operating income $7,647M / US segment total revenue (incl. membership fees), derived. Total company was 3.85% (11,685/303,154).
fiscal_years.avg_store_sqft_note: US: 96.6M sq ft / 647, derived. Company-wide disclosed average is ~148,000.
fiscal_years.private_label_note: Kirkland Signature share of sales is not disclosed in the 10-K.

fiscal_years.om_basis: US segment OI 6,878 / US total revenue, derived. Total company 3.77%.

fiscal_years.om_basis: US segment OI 6,217 / US total revenue, derived. Total company 3.65%.

WMT.fiscal_year_end: January 31. FY2026 = year ended 2026-01-31 (the company's own label; comparable in timing to KR, ACI and TGT 'FY2025'). The latest quarter is Q3 FY2027 (ended 2026-10-31).
WMT.scope: WALMART U.S. SEGMENT only (excludes Sam's Club U.S. and International). Includes walmart.com eCommerce and advertising.
WMT.product_focus: Mass merchandiser: supercenters (~178k sq ft average) with full grocery plus general merchandise and pharmacy, discount stores, and Neighborhood Markets. Grocery is ~59% of Walmart U.S. net sales.
WMT.comp_definition: CALENDAR comparable sales (10-K, fiscal calendar): stores open for the previous 12 months, including remodels, relocations, expansions and conversions, PLUS eCommerce sales (all digitally initiated sales, including store-fulfilled omnichannel and certain ecosystem offerings such as advertising). Reported WITH fuel; the fuel impact is shown separately and was 0.0 / (0.1) / (0.1) pp. The quarterly release uses retail 4-5-4 calendar comps 'ex. fuel'.

skus_per_store.note: Supercenter only: 'the Supercenter carries 120,000 items' (Walmart CFO Brett Biggs, Talk Business & Politics, 2019-03-28). Dated and not from a filing; treat as indicative.

fiscal_years.om_basis: Walmart U.S. segment OI $25,158M / segment net sales (company-reported %)

TGT.fiscal_year_end: Saturday nearest Jan 31. FY2025 = 52 weeks ended 2026-01-31. FY2024 = 2025-02-01. FY2023 = 53 weeks ended 2024-02-03.
TGT.scope: Total company (US only). GROCERY IS ONLY PART OF SALES: Food & beverage was 23.5% of merchandise sales in FY2025.
TGT.product_focus: General-merchandise discount department stores with a grocery section (dry grocery, dairy, frozen, limited fresh). Strong owned brands (e.g. Good & Gather). Pharmacies are operated by CVS, so their sales are not Target's.
TGT.comp_definition: Comparable sales = all Merchandise Sales (stores AND digitally originated), except sales from stores open less than 13 months or closed. Excludes non-merchandise revenue (advertising, credit-card profit sharing). No fuel.

WMK.fiscal_year_end: Last Saturday in December. FY2025 = 52 weeks ended 2025-12-27. FY2022 was 53 weeks.
WMK.scope: Total company (Mid-Atlantic). Net sales include fuel (~5% of sales).
WMK.product_focus: Conventional Mid-Atlantic supermarkets (~49,000 sq ft average) with full perishables, pharmacy and fuel, self-distribution (~52%) and its own dairy and meat plants.
WMK.comp_definition: Comparable store sales: a new store becomes comparable after five full fiscal quarters. Relocated and expanded stores are INCLUDED. Planned dispositions are excluded. Retail food stores only. Reported both INCLUDING fuel and EXCLUDING fuel; we use EX-FUEL as the headline. The FY2023 figure is adjusted for the 53rd week in 2022.
WMK.restatement_warning: The FY2025 10-K restated FY2024 and FY2023 (overstated inventory and understated cost of goods sold at a meat manufacturing plant). The figures below are the restated values from the FY2025 10-K and XBRL.
